text.p: This week's new products include new beverages, magazines, personal care products and additions to a celebrity clothing line.
Campbell Soup Co. will launch next month a new line of juices, joining the company's $300 million V8 juice brand.
"V8 Splash" combines tropical fruits such as pineapple, kiwi, lime and mango with carrot juice for a beverage that provides 100 percent of the recommended daily amounts of vitamins A and C.
Campbell also will introduce a line of "Healthy Request V8" juice, which contains 25 percent less sodium than regular V8.
The packaged foods company said the new juice lines will have a $20 million national advertising campaign, free sample giveaways and other consumer promotions.

"V8 Splash" will come in three flavors -- Tropical Blend, Strawberry Kiwi and Citrus Blend. The 16-ounce glass bottle will cost about 99 cents and the 46-ounce plastic bottles will sell for about $2.39.

"Healthy Request V8" juice, which contains 100 percent of the recommended daily amounts of vitamins A, C and E, will be available in 46-ounce cans, 46-ounce plastic bottles and 5.5-ounce six pack cans. Prices will range from $1.79 to $2.39.
Joining the ever expanding world of magazines dedicated to the world of fine living is Appellation, a Napa, Calif.-based magazine that specialised in "Wine Country living."
Updated from an earlier incarnation, Appellation in the May-June issue looks at Chile, with numerous vinyards producing world-class wines.
Other articles concern foods that go well with particular wines, places to stay and eat in various wine-producing areas around the world and personal reflections on the world of wine.
The magazine will be published six times a year. It has a newsstand price of $3.95 ($4.95 Canadian).
For subscription information, call 1-800-799-2679. The magazine's editorial and design offices are at 1040 Main Street, Suite 100, Napa, Calif. 94559.
Delta Burke, who recently launched a pattern collection with Butterick Patterns, will have her signature clothing line featured in the Fall 1997, 16W and Up, J.C Penney catalogue.
The catalogue will show additions to the Delta Burke Design line, including casual sportswear, fashion jewelry and belts.

"The new union with JC Penney's will both broaden Delta Burke Design distribution and enable 'real-sized' women to more easily purchase Delta Burke Design," the former star of televison's "Designing Women," said.
Items in the Fall 1997, 16W and Up catalogue range in price from $15 to $70.
The catalogue will be mailed to customers in July.
Procter & Gamble's Secret, the nation's largest selling brand of anti-perspirants and deodorants, will introduce Secret Sheer Dry, a clear anti-perspirant and deodorant for women.
Secret Sheer Dry will be introduced in June.

Other new products to be introduced later this year by Procter & Gamble include Old Spice High Endurance, which will have improved deodorant protection and a "Pure Sport" fragrance, replacing "Musk High Endurance."
Sure Clear Dry will be marketed in a new formulation involving a gel solid technology.
Secret Sheer Dry will appear on store shelves in late June and should be available nationwide in July. It will come in both regular and powerder fresh scents in 1.6 oz. and 2.6 oz. sizes.
Suggested retail prices range from $1.89 to $2.79 depending on size.
Bruegger's Corp., the nation-wide bagel retailer, has introduced what it calls the first significant change to the fresh-baked bagel in 300 years.
Bruegger's Hot Stuffed Bagels is a bagel without a hole, filled with egg, bacon and cheese; spinach and cheese; or Italian cheese Supreme.
The stuffed bagels are filled before baking.
The bagel was said to have been invented in 1683 in Vienna. Bruegger's said the stuffed bagels are currently being introduced.
